criteria.browser_entry_hook: Leave the guard untouched and have the paired browser bundle entry register the htmx:config:request listener whenever the live document carries a generation slot. No regeneration and no re-pinning, but htmx request policy now lives in two places: the guard keeps target and response duties while the browser entry owns the identity header.
criteria.exempt_form: Build no htmx header channel and leave form mounts outside enforcement. Stale htmx pages keep posting through without a handshake while JSON actions still refuse across generations; the least code, at the cost of a form path that never fails closed.
criteria.guard_injection: Teach the owned htmx guard, which already self-installs on every htmx page, to copy the live document data-can-generation slot into detail.ctx.request.headers on htmx:config:request. The C-E policy mechanism carries the C-H identity; costs guardgen regeneration plus the six documented re-pin spots.

htmx_channel.instructions: Which channel should carry the paired-build generation on htmx-driven form requests?

criteria.new_identity: Introduce a dedicated catalogue failure identity for the mismatch, threaded through the checker and the emitter so every action failure bound gains a member and every match site handles it. The refusal reads as its own case everywhere, at the price of a catalogue slice plus updating all declared bounds and handlers.
criteria.phase_value: Keep the refusal inside the existing transport family: fetchJsonAction reports a distinct generation_mismatch outcome and createJsonActionFetch lowers it to http::transport_failed with phase generation. No catalogue, checker, or emitter change; the E04 timeout and cancelled phases set the precedent for runtime-only phase growth.

lowering.instructions: How should the browser action client expose a server generation refusal to Can programs?

criteria.always_pin_uniform: Every server pins its manifest buildID at startup and refuses every action mount, JSON, form, and document alike, when the header is missing, malformed, or unequal. Curl, tests, and companion callers must all send the header, and plain navigations to document mounts stop working.
criteria.paired_pin_json_only: Pin the generation on paired builds only and enforce it on JSON mounts alone. Form mounts stay outside the check, so htmx needs no channel change and existing form flows cannot break, but stale form pages post across generations without refusal.
criteria.paired_pin_selective: Pin the serving generation only for paired builds with a readable manifest, leaving unpaired servers exactly as today. Enforce the header on JSON and form mounts; exempt document mounts, since navigations cannot send custom headers and no document mount exists in any program.

scope.instructions: Which servers should pin their generation, and which action mounts should refuse on mismatch?

state.client: The browser JSON action path runs fetchJsonAction over native fetch and classifies into ActionFetchResult kinds ok, transport, aborted, timeout, codec, and unexpected_status; createJsonActionFetch then lowers those into six fixed declared failure identities including http::transport_failed with its str phase. One genuine domain case already answers 409, grid_conflict, so only the byte-exact mismatch shape may map to the refusal, never a domain 409. The E04 budget work grew the phase vocabulary at runtime, adding timeout and cancelled with no catalogue change.
state.fixed: Outside this consultation and already settled: the 409 shape {schemaVersion 1, kind can.generation-mismatch, serverGeneration 64-hex}; the page slot as data-can-generation on the paired script tag spliced by pairDocument; the request header name can-generation; symmetric mismatch comparison with rollback refusing exactly like rollout; asset routes carrying no check; a blocking refresh prompt with no silent reload and no retried action. Zero external users exist, so no legacy compatibility burden applies.
state.handshake: A paired Can deploy binds one server generation, the 64-hex manifest buildID, to one browser build. Every served text/html document names its serving generation in a data-can-generation slot on the paired script tag, and every action request from live-document logic is expected to echo that value in a can-generation header. Any inequality, including a missing or malformed header, fails closed with a typed 409 mismatch answered before any action logic runs, and the app answers with a blocking refresh prompt.
state.htmx: Form actions reach the server through htmx 4.0.0, vendored and pinned, which fires htmx:config:request with a mutable detail.ctx.request.headers object before each request. The owned guard module already self-installs on every htmx page and owns target, response, and swap policy; it is zero-import and ships as generated bytes refreshed by guardgen with six documented integrity re-pin spots. Plain navigations, including refreshes and address-bar loads of document pages, cannot attach custom headers; they always fetch the serving generation current document.
state.server: Emitted servers mount JSON, form, and document actions onto the router through createActionRoutes mount, mountForm, and mountDocument, and dispatch matches each request against the compiled capture table. The assets root handed to createAssets is the serving generation directory, so manifest.json with the buildID sits beside it. Unpaired builds serve actions to curl, tests, and non-browser callers that know nothing of the handshake, and no program today mounts a document action.
